feature: historical price oracle, cache, and transaction enrichment

commands.summary: 3 test files; 48 tests passed (gen-2..gen-4 hardening: impossible full-timestamp rejection, process-level single-flight dedup, poisoned-close-not-cached, offset->UTC-day keying, trailing-garbage rejection). Expected warning logs exercised the network-throw and oracle-throw best-effort paths.

adversarialCases.scenario: HTTP 429 and network rejection from CoinGecko
adversarialCases.expected: null result (UNKNOWN semantics), never a synthetic zero price
adversarialCases.testRef: apps/backend/src/indexer/historical-price-oracle.spec.ts :: CoinGeckoHistoricalPriceOracle.priceAt > returns null (UNKNOWN, never 0) on a non-ok HTTP response; returns null on a network throw

adversarialCases.scenario: ERC721/ERC1155, unsupported chain, and malformed date
adversarialCases.testRef: apps/backend/src/indexer/historical-price-oracle.spec.ts :: CoinGeckoHistoricalPriceOracle.priceAt > returns null for NFTs, unsupported chains, and malformed dates without fetching

adversarialCases.scenario: HTTP 200 response with no in-day price points
adversarialCases.expected: null confirmed no-data result; distinct source path from non-OK/throw lookup failure and never coerced to 0
adversarialCases.testRef: apps/backend/src/indexer/historical-price-oracle.spec.ts :: summarizeDailyClose > returns null for a 200-response with no in-window data (confirmed no-data, not failure); CoinGeckoHistoricalPriceOracle.priceAt > returns null (UNKNOWN, never 0) on a non-ok HTTP response

adversarialCases.scenario: Repository has a historical close before enrichment
adversarialCases.expected: oracle calls = 0 and cached close is used
adversarialCases.testRef: apps/backend/src/indexer/historical-price-enrichment.service.spec.ts :: HistoricalPriceEnrichmentService.enrich > does not touch the oracle when the price is already cached (cache-first)

adversarialCases.scenario: Two same-asset, same-day ERC20 rows with quantities 1 and 3 at unit close 1,000,000 KRW
adversarialCases.expected: one oracle call; fiat_value equals unit close multiplied by each quantity
adversarialCases.testRef: apps/backend/src/indexer/historical-price-enrichment.service.spec.ts :: HistoricalPriceEnrichmentService.enrich > consults the oracle at most once per (asset, day) and caches the close

adversarialCases.scenario: Null lookup and a row already carrying ESTIMATED fiat value
adversarialCases.expected: null lookup stays UNKNOWN/null rather than 0; existing fiat_value and status are unchanged with zero oracle calls
adversarialCases.testRef: apps/backend/src/indexer/historical-price-enrichment.service.spec.ts :: HistoricalPriceEnrichmentService.enrich > leaves the basis UNKNOWN on a null lookup and never coerces to 0; never overwrites an already-priced row (mock path is untouched)

adversarialCases.scenario: Oracle throws while processing an enrich batch
adversarialCases.expected: batch resolves; affected row remains UNKNOWN
adversarialCases.testRef: apps/backend/src/indexer/historical-price-enrichment.service.spec.ts :: HistoricalPriceEnrichmentService.enrich > does not fail the batch when the oracle throws (best-effort)

adversarialCases.expected: dayWindow returns null via UTC round-trip; no wrong-day pricing
adversarialCases.testRef: historical-price-oracle.spec.ts :: dayWindow > rejects impossible calendar dates instead of normalizing them

adversarialCases.expected: endpointKind returns null; never routed to a mismatched endpoint
adversarialCases.testRef: historical-price-oracle.spec.ts :: endpointKind > whitelists only native (null contract) and ERC20 (non-empty contract)
historical-price-oracle.spec.ts :: summarizeDailyClose > rejects non-positive and blank close values

adversarialCases.scenario: unpriced row arriving with stale RESOLVED status; failed lookup
adversarialCases.expected: price_status forced to UNKNOWN, fiat_value stays null
adversarialCases.testRef: historical-price-enrichment.service.spec.ts :: forces price_status UNKNOWN for an unpriced row even if it arrived non-UNKNOWN

adversarialCases.scenario: concurrent miss: our put is a no-op loser, a winner already stored 900,000
adversarialCases.expected: post-put re-read applies the winner (900,000), not our losing 111,111 lookup
adversarialCases.testRef: historical-price-enrichment.service.spec.ts :: applies the canonical persisted close, not a losing concurrent lookup

adversarialCases.expected: rejected; fiat_value stays null, status UNKNOWN
dateOf validates the raw YYYY-MM-DD prefix before Date.parse; never priced on the normalized March day (0 oracle calls, UNKNOWN)
adversarialCases.testRef: historical-price-enrichment.service.spec.ts :: rejects an impossible full timestamp instead of normalizing it to a wrong day

adversarialCases.scenario: two concurrent enrich() calls on the singleton service for the same key, both held in-flight
adversarialCases.expected: one shared oracle lookup (process-level single-flight); both rows priced correctly
adversarialCases.testRef: historical-price-enrichment.service.spec.ts :: coalesces concurrent enrich calls into one oracle lookup per key (single-flight)

adversarialCases.expected: validated before put; not written to cache (stays retryable, not permanent UNKNOWN)
adversarialCases.testRef: historical-price-enrichment.service.spec.ts :: does not cache a poisoned oracle close

adversarialCases.expected: keyed by UTC day 2025-01-02, not the raw local prefix 2025-01-03
adversarialCases.testRef: historical-price-enrichment.service.spec.ts :: keys an offset timestamp by its UTC day, not the raw local date prefix

adversarialCases.scenario: valid date prefix with trailing garbage (2025-01-03XYZ)
adversarialCases.expected: full-string Date.parse fails -> null; row stays UNKNOWN, 0 oracle calls
adversarialCases.testRef: historical-price-enrichment.service.spec.ts :: rejects a valid-prefix timestamp with trailing garbage

endToEnd.summary: 19 IndexerService tests passed in the same invocation; its harness constructs HistoricalPriceEnrichmentService with MockHistoricalPriceOracle and MockHistoricalPriceRepository.
